text:
Predicates:
Book(x) ::: x is a book.
Contains(x, y) ::: x contains y.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Reads(x, y) ::: x reads y.
Gains(x, y) ::: x gains y.
Knowledge(x) ::: x is knowledge.
Smarter(x) ::: x is smarter.
Premises:
∀x (Book(x) → Contains(x, knowledge)) ::: Books contain tons of knowledge.
∀x ∀y (Person(x) ∧ Book(y) ∧ Reads(x, y) → Gains(x, knowledge)) ::: When a person reads a book, that person gains knowledge.
∀x (Person(x) ∧ Gains(x, knowledge) → Smarter(x)) ::: If a person gains knowledge, they become smarter.
Person(harry) ∧ Book(walden) ∧ Author(walden, henryThoreau) ∧ Reads(harry, walden) ::: Harry read the book 'Walden' by Henry Thoreau.
Conclusion:
∀x (Person(x) ∧ Smarter(x) → ∃y (Gains(x, y) ∧ Knowledge(y))) ::: A smarter person has gained knowledge.
